## 1. What is being burned

| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Sprint | 2 (2026-11-02 → 2026-11-15) |
| Committed scope | 82 story points (provisional; team velocity unknown) |
| Remaining at sprint start | 82 |
| Remaining at 2026-11-05 | **8** |
| Remaining at sprint end (2026-11-15) | **5** |
| Burned | 77 SP |

> **Honesty note.** All 74 burned points were completed by the implementation harness in one working session
> on 2026-11-05 (backend slice, tests, UI build, documents, decks, course artifacts). They are **not** team
> velocity and must not be used to forecast human capacity. Days 2026-11-02 → 2026-11-04 show zero progress
> because the repository did not exist before 2026-11-05.

The 8 remaining points are deliberately the ones a machine cannot finish: a human process audit (S2-16),
real 10–30 minute footage validation (S2-17) and the sprint review/retrospective (S2-18).

## 3. Interpretation

- The remaining 29 SP are concentrated in UI completion, the Requirements & Design deck, installation/user
  manuals, real-video validation and the sprint review/retrospective.
- Because no human capacity is declared, the shape of the remaining line is **unknown**. The first real
  data point will be 2026-11-06; until then this is a scope chart, not a capacity forecast.
- If the UI or the deck slips past **2026-11-09**, the deck upload is the higher priority (hard course
  deadline), and the UI can land on 11-13 without breaking the MVP gate.
- A flat line for two consecutive days is an escalation trigger for the mid-sprint review on 11-11.

## 4. Updating this file

1. At the end of each working day, add the actual remaining SP from the Sprint Backlog (count only `Done`).
2. Regenerate the chart:
   ```powershell
   .\.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts\render_burndown.py
   ```
3. Record why points moved (which tasks), not just the number. Never smooth the curve.
